transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lila (Rivermark Head of AI), Tom (Platform), Anita (FinOps), Jamal (Security), Speaker 6

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Rivermark is evaluating Redwood Console to get per-route telemetry and cost breakdowns for their LLM-powered risk engine. They want visibility into token-level spend, per-route latency, and controls for fallback to cheaper variants. SE walked through routes dashboard, cost lenses, and Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization). Security questions on VPC, KMS, and audit logs. Next: pilot scope and benchmark spreadsheet.

Topics:
- Current stack and constraints
- Per-route dashboards and filters
- Cost breakdown (tokens, kv cache effects, batching)
- Dedicated vs hosted decision criteria
- Security / VPC / KMS / audit logs
- Pilot next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll hand it to Diego to drive the console tour and then we'll answer any infra/security questions.
[00:05] Diego: Cool, hi all. Um, so quick context I know Rivermark has a risk scoring flow and a chat-based analyst assistant, correct? Lila?
[00:12] Lila: Yeah that's right, we have two primary routes — the scoring API that does a 2k token average context and the analyst chat which is more like 6k with history.
[00:19] Tom: And we're running mostly on GCP, want to keep data residency in US-east and keep latency under 250ms p95 if possible.
[00:26] Anita: Important for us is visibility — we need per-team chargebacks and to show savings if we move to Redwood versus building our own infra.
[00:33] Diego: Great, I'll show the Console and specifically the Routes view, which surfaces per-route usage, latency, token counts, and cost attribution.
[00:40] [01:05] Diego: (screen share) okay here's the main routes table — you can see route names, model pinned, avg latency, cost, and a heatmap of token size. You can click into a route to see a time-series and top prompts.
[01:20] Lila: That model column — is that the live model or the variant? We sometimes fall back to a quantized model for cheaper runs.
[01:27] Diego: Good Q — we show both the resident model and recent fallbacks. There's a small icons bar that indicates if a route used cached prefixes, or if a fallback happened to a quantized variant. The console will report fallbacks and approximate cost delta.
[01:40] Anita: How accurate is the per-token cost? Our FinOps team needs a near-exact mapping to invoice.
[01:45] Maya: Quick note — the hosted pricing has per-token rates but for Dedicated we give committed pricing with route-level allocation; the Console models unit economics using the actual kernel/quant profile so it's a close model, not a theoretical estimate.
[01:58] Diego: For example here, this route shows 32k tokens total this week, breakdown by prompt/completion, and how much was saved due to prefix caching — about 18% lower.
[02:12] Tom: Can you show the cost lens that breaks out kernel execution vs batching overhead vs infra?
[02:18] Diego: Yep — switch to the Cost Breakdown panel. (short pause) So we split cost into Token compute (model kernels), Memory (kv cache hotness), IO overhead, and orchestration (eg autoscale warmup). You can toggle a view to show cost per-token or cost per-request.
[02:35] [03:00] Jamal: On security: do you surface audit logs for each call? We need per-token audit trails for compliance.
[03:06] Maya: We keep an audit trail — request metadata, user token, model version and route mapping — logs can be shipped to your SIEM or kept in customer-controlled storage in Private deployments. There is SAML SSO and RBAC integration.
[03:20] Jamal: And KMS? Our keys are in HSM and we can't share raw context.
[03:24] Diego: We support KMS integrations and the Private control plane can be run in your VPC; the inference plane stays within your network for on-prem or VPC peering setups.
[03:32] Lila: If we go Dedicated, do we still get the Console cost suggestions like batching and quantization?
[03:36] Diego: Yes — Optimize runs workload profiling and suggests batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, and quantization levels even for Dedicated pools. It's just the runtime that lives in your capacity.
[03:46] Anita: Could you show an example suggestion?
[03:49] Diego: Sure — open the Optimize tab. Here the system recommends enabling dynamic batching up to 16 requests for the scoring route and lowering precision to 4-bit (GPTQ) for older checkpoints. It also quantifies expected savings — e.g., 2.4x token-cost reduction at the expense of a small quality delta the eval flagged.
[04:11] Lila: Hmm, that quality delta — is that measured against our evals? We have specific accuracy gates for risk scoring.
[04:18] Diego: We can ingest your eval set. In the Console you can bind an eval set per-route; Optimize will show expected ROUGE-like metrics or custom metrics you define.
[04:27] [05:10] Speaker 6: (background) are there rate limits per route?
[05:12] Maya: Yes, you can set route-level quotas and burst policies, and have a fallback policy that either queue, degrade to smaller model, or reject.
[05:20] Tom: Show us the fallback policy UI — we want automatic fallback to a cheaper variant before queuing.
[05:24] Diego: (navigates) here — policy engine. You can set SLO targets (p95 latency), and if latency spikes the policy will first try a cheaper quantized model in the same pool, then if that fails fallback to a cross-region replica. You can also pin certain requests to never fallback for sensitive traffic.
[05:40] Anita: On billing — can we get monthly route-level invoices that map to our teams?
[05:44] Maya: Yes, there's a cost export. You can map routes to billing tags and export CSVs or push to BigQuery. We also have a FinOps dashboard that shows spend by route, team, and model.
[05:55] [07:00] Lila: Performance — you showed p95 under 250ms earlier, is that realistic for 6k context?
[07:05] Diego: For the chat route with 6k history, p95 of 250ms is ambitious on typical A100-sized instances; we usually hit ~350-500ms depending on model size. For lower latency you can use pinned smaller model or quantized variants. There was a note that your latency target might require Dedicated capacity and locality.
[07:22] Tom: So contention and batching windows matter. Can we cap batching to ensure low tail?
[07:26] Diego: Yep you can set max batching latency (ms) and preferred batch size. Optimize will suggest values that balance cost and p95.
[07:35] Jamal: Data residency — can we ensure logs and KV cache stay in our VPC?
[07:39] Maya: For Private deployments yes, full control. For Hosted but in your region we keep logs in designated region; for full isolation we recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed storage.
[07:50] [10:00] Diego: (drilling into route details) here's per-route trace view — you can see a waterfall for token timings, kernel time, kv lookup, and network. That helps pinpoint whether latency is kernel-limited or IO-bound.
[10:12] Lila: Nice, can the waterfall correlate to specific prompt templates?
[10:16] Diego: Yes, top prompts are shown; you can group by template and see cost/latency by template. There's also a prompt-heatmap for token length distribution.
[10:28] Anita: For our CFO, a single number comparison to current infra would be useful. Can you produce a savings estimate if we move 3 routes to Dedicated?
[10:36] Maya: We can; Diego will run a projection that uses your traffic histogram and our kernel profiles. It will show monthly cost delta and expected ROI period.
[10:44] [12:00] Diego: (shares quick mock spreadsheet) here's a sample — shows tokens, avg seq len, p50/p95 latency, and three cost columns: Hosted rate, Dedicated committed rate, and self-host estimated infra. We also show sensitivity to quantization and caching.
[12:18] Tom: About self-host — we looked at Anthropic and also internal self-host. How do you compare?
[12:24] Maya: The tradeoff is control versus operational burden. Redwood aims to give predictable economics and safety nets (auto-fallback, rollouts, tracing). For raw price, if you operate at extreme scale self-host might be cheaper but you accept more ops risk.
[12:38] [15:00] Lila: One more — does Console let us tag requests for compliance classification so certain PII never leaves the model?
[15:06] Diego: You can attach metadata flags to requests and set route policies to redact or skip storage. For sensitive flows we recommend Private or Dedicated with strict key management.
[15:18] Jamal: We need a sample architecture diagram for how Private deployment looks in our VPC for our security review.
[15:22] Maya: We'll attach a VPC deployment diagram and the VPC checklist in the follow-up email.
[15:28] [20:00] Diego: Quick demo of Alerts — Console can trigger alerts on abnormal spend per-route, regressions in eval metrics, and latency spikes. Alerts integrate with PagerDuty and Slack.
[20:12] Anita: Good, FinOps wants an alert if route spend exceeds forecast by 15% month-over-month.
[20:18] Diego: Noted, you can create that alert now and set escalation.
[20:25] Lila: Any limitations on large-context KV cache? Our chat needs 20k history sometimes.
[20:30] Diego: Large KV is supported but memory pressure and latency tradeoffs apply. Optimize will recommend sharding and TTLs; beyond a point we recommend session summarization.
[20:45] [30:00] (brief side conversation; background chatter)
[30:40] Tom: For pilot scope — we propose three routes: scoring, analyst-chat (reduced history mode), and a nightly-batch reranking job.
[30:46] Maya: Sounds good. Pilot success criteria?
[30:50] Anita: Cost reduction of 30% vs current self-hosted estimate, p95 latency under 350ms for scoring, and no quality regressions on eval set.
[30:58] Lila: Also security signoff with keys and audit logs.
[31:05] Diego: We'll instrument the pilot with extra tracing and produce the per-route CSV exports daily.
[31:10] Maya: I'll send the pilot contract and pricing options after Diego's projection spreadsheet.
[31:15] [40:00] (Diego runs a small live benchmark with synthetic traffic)
[40:30] Diego: Running 60 RPS with 2k context on the scoring route — p50 ~ 78ms, p95 ~ 320ms, token throughput shown in dashboard. Note, your real traffic may vary.
[40:45] Tom: Those p95 numbers look okay for the scoring route.
[40:50] Lila: For chat we should test the 6k case separately.
[40:54] Diego: Agreed — we'll include that in the benchmark run for the pilot.
[41:00] [47:00] (QA and clarifications)
[47:12] Jamal: Final ask — can audit logs be retained for 2 years and can we have export hooks?
[47:18] Maya: Yes, retention policy is configurable for Private; for hosted we have standard 90 days but enterprise add-ons extend to 2 years and you can export to your S3/GCS.
[47:30] Anita: Any network hop concerns for Dedicated?
[47:34] Diego: If Dedicated is in your cloud account (private VPC), hop count is minimal. We provide diagrams for peering and for on-prem.
[47:45] Maya: Ok to recap — Diego will run the per-route cost projection and benchmarks, Maya will send SOC2/security assets and pricing, Rivermark to confirm pilot routes and provide traffic histograms.
[47:58] Lila: Sounds good.
[48:02] Tom: We'll aim to get traffic histograms by Monday.
[48:08] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with the pilot proposal and schedule the kickoff. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
